monitored_sources.name: European Commission AI Act implementation page
monitored_sources.status_change_summary: Official page presents phased AI Act application, GPAI obligations, high-risk transition timing, and 2026 simplification/omnibus implementation posture.
monitored_sources.archive_action_required: Keep AI Act crosswalk dated; do not treat compliance filings as proof of AI-subject authority or live receipt satisfaction.

monitored_sources.name: European Commission Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content
monitored_sources.status_change_summary: June 2026 transparency code adds marking/labelling implementation vocabulary for Article 50 obligations, including deployer and provider sections.
monitored_sources.archive_action_required: Route generated-content marking to provenance/publication controls; do not let provenance labels stand in for representative authority, subject authorization, or admissible receipt class.

monitored_sources.name: NIST AI RMF and GenAI/Critical Infrastructure profiles
monitored_sources.status_change_summary: NIST continues to position AI RMF as voluntary risk-management guidance, with GenAI profile and 2026 critical-infrastructure concept note as control vocabulary.
monitored_sources.archive_action_required: Use NIST terms for safety-case controls and incident monitoring only; never substitute RMF conformance for personhood status, subject consent, or live artifact proof.

monitored_sources.name: Model Context Protocol specification security and trust section
monitored_sources.status_change_summary: Latest MCP spec page says MCP enables powerful arbitrary data access and code-execution paths, requires explicit user consent/control, treats tool descriptions as untrusted unless from trusted servers, and says hosts must obtain consent before tool invocation.
monitored_sources.archive_action_required: Keep MCP tool/resource/authorization success outside receipt authority; rev0217 evidence-drop/admission graph requires evidence-drop/LEAP/custody lineage before any response/intake/import path.

monitored_sources.name: A2A Protocol official documentation
monitored_sources.status_change_summary: Official A2A docs describe an open protocol for communication and interoperability between opaque agentic applications; they distinguish MCP for agent-to-tool communication from A2A for agent-to-agent discovery, delegation, and result sharing.
monitored_sources.archive_action_required: Treat A2A discovery, agent cards, task states, and authentication as transport/coordination evidence only; rev0209 requires evidence-drop/LEAP/custody lineage and class-specific authority before downstream records.

monitored_sources.name: MCP security design considerations
monitored_sources.status_change_summary: Security guidance treats MCP-based agentic systems as a dynamic trust-boundary and tool/supply-chain risk surface.
monitored_sources.archive_action_required: Keep protocol-pivot tests critical until the first live artifact path proves authority, non-host retention, and verifier outputs separately from relay transport.

monitored_sources.name: Sigstore/Rekor signing and transparency log documentation
monitored_sources.status_change_summary: Sigstore/Rekor documentation describes signed metadata, timestamped signing events, artifact hash/public-key/signature material, inclusion proof, and append-only transparency-log auditing.
monitored_sources.archive_action_required: Use Rekor/timestamp evidence as authenticity/timing support only; rev0209 still requires LEAP, raw custody, authority, and independence before import credit.

monitored_sources.name: IETF RFC 9334 Remote ATtestation procedureS architecture
monitored_sources.status_change_summary: RATS supplies attester/evidence/verifier/relying-party vocabulary for deciding whether a peer is in an intended operating state, but it is informational architecture rather than personhood authority proof.
monitored_sources.archive_action_required: Use RATS vocabulary to refine verifier-adapter roles and runtime attestation records; keep attestation evidence separate from receipt-class authority and live-floor credit.

monitored_sources.name: Sigstore/Rekor transparency-log and signing documentation
monitored_sources.status_change_summary: Rekor transparency logs support append-only integrity monitoring and verifier identity monitoring, but do not by themselves establish class-specific authority, subject authorization, or raw counterparty custody.
monitored_sources.archive_action_required: Use log inclusion and signature verification as verifier-adapter inputs after evidence-drop quarantine; do not let log/provenance metadata bypass raw payload custody or LEAP.

risk_decisions.decision: Keep current-law/protocol watch as a dated object, not prose-only crosswalk text.
risk_decisions.why: Fast-moving legal and agent-protocol sources can stale artifact-admission and governance crosswalk assumptions within a few releases.

risk_decisions.decision: Treat protocol authentication and content provenance as insufficient for subject authorization or receipt-floor credit.
risk_decisions.why: Transport security, agent discovery, and provenance labels can be true while authority, consent, non-host retention, or class-specific receipt proof is absent.

risk_decisions.decision: Insert LEAP before response creation whenever protocol, provenance, signature, or attestation evidence is present but raw custody or authority slots are incomplete.
risk_decisions.why: The current protocol ecosystem can produce high-confidence transport and authenticity artifacts that are still not live receipt authority or independent evidence.

public_summary: rev0217 carries forward the dated law/protocol watch as a non-receipt governance snapshot while adding pilot and status-denominator controls; it creates no authority, custody, or live-floor credit.
